output.brief: The remote promotion gap is mostly a tenure effect, not a location effect. Remote hiring only opened widely in July 2024, so 215 of 340 remote staff started after March 2025. Only 32% of remote staff meet the policy's 18-months-in-level rule, against 74% of office staff. Among eligible people, nomination and approval rates are almost the same: remote 20.0% promoted, office 21.1%. Applying office rates to the remote tenure mix predicts 8.2%, and the observed rate is 7.6%. Remote staff are not leaving faster (10.9% vs 11.6%). The gap also appears in every job family, so job mix doesn't explain it. The eligible remote group is only 110 people, so a modest real difference can't be ruled out. Manager comments suggest some uneven access to visible work, but that isn't measured. Don't adopt the three-day office rule. It would penalise about 180 people hired on home-based contracts, and the data don't support it. Put it on hold. Change reporting to compare eligible staff only, and re-check at FY2027. Also measure stretch assignments, and explain the promotion criteria to remote staff, since their understanding scores are lower.
